name: Binaural Study Hall
description: Classical music for studying, reading and writing, built for headphones: a prelude over a soft alpha beat, a string quartet seated around you, a sarabande over a pad that spreads from the centre to all around you, a larghetto whose strings breathe apart in cents, a slowly rotating chorale, an etude whose brightness wanders between the ears, a two-part invention with one voice in each ear, a nocturne in a wide, quiet reading room, a baroque allegretto over a beta beat and a harp minuet over a delta drone to close the books. Each sketch is a short complete piece of about two minutes: an introduction, the main section with a varied repeat, a slower final chord and a real stop. Slow tempos, gentle levels and nothing sudden; each sketch explains its trick in the comments. Headphones on, volume low.
author: Claude, for Tartlet

sketches.name: Alpha Prelude
sketches.description: A prelude of broken chords in C, the same in both ears, over a cello and a quiet 10 Hz binaural drone in the alpha range. The cello and drone open alone, the prelude plays twice (the second time an octave up) and a slower held C ends the piece. The beat forms only between the ears, so on speakers you hear a plain drone. The player asks before playing, as with any steady pulse.

sketches.name: Seated Quartet
sketches.description: An andante in F for string quartet, seated in a semicircle in front of you as on a concert stage: first violin far left, second violin left of centre, viola right of centre and cello on the right. The viola and cello open, the theme plays twice (the second time an octave up), the viola sings the tune from its seat in an episode, the theme returns and the quartet closes slowly on F.

sketches.name: Sarabande in Phase
sketches.description: A harpsichord sarabande in D minor, with its weight on the second beat, sits in the centre of your head while a string pad underneath steps from in phase to 90 and 180 degrees, two bars at a time, spreading from a point into a haze. The sarabande plays with its repeat, then as a double with every note struck twice, then once more before a final D minor chord where the pad comes back to a point. On speakers the 180-degree bars of the pad nearly vanish.

sketches.name: Larghetto in Cents
sketches.description: A slow piano larghetto in G over strings whose ears drift apart in cents and back again: 3 cents beats slowly, 8 shimmers and 15 widens like a larger section. The strings open alone, the piano sings three times (an octave higher the second time) and the strings settle back to 3 cents over a held G. The piano and cello stay true in the centre.
sketches.source:
setcpm(50/4)

// The strings alone, the larghetto three times (an octave higher in the middle), then a held G
song("intro@4 larghetto@8 larghetto'@8 larghetto@8 coda@4", "once")
// Steady, then a ritardando over the last four bars
tempomap("0:12.5 28:12.5 32:9")

// earsh raises the right ear and lowers the left by half the value each
// The strings breathe out and back in: 3, 8, 15, then 8 cents, two bars each
strings: note("<[g2,d3,b3,d4] [e2,b2,g3,b3] [c3,g3,e4] [d3,a3,f#4]>").slow(2)
  .s("sawtooth").unison(2).detune(.1).earsh("<3 3 8 8 15 15 8 8>")
  .lpf(1200).attack(2).sustain(1).release(3).room(.7).size(.9).gain(.12)
  .exceptSections("coda")

// The piano sings in the centre, the same in both ears: G, Em, C, D7
piano: note("<[b4@3 a4] [g4@4] [g4@2 b4 e5] [d5@4] [e5@3 d5] [c5@2 e4@2] [f#4@2 a4 d5] [c5@2 a4@2]>")
  .s("triangle").timbre("soft").attack(.005).decay(1.6).sustain(.1).release(1.6)
  .room(.6).size(.8).gain(.26)
  .sections("larghetto").variant(x => x.add(12).gain(.2))

// The cello holds the roots
cello: note("<g1 e2 c2 d2>").slow(2).s("sawtooth").vib(4.5).vibdepth(.08)
  .lpf(600).attack(1).sustain(.8).release(2).room(.5).gain(.18)
  .exceptSections("coda")

// The strings settle back to 3 cents over a held G, with the cello beneath
final: note("[g1,g2,d3,b3,d4]").slow(4).s("sawtooth").unison(2).detune(.1).earsh(3)
  .lpf(1000).attack(1).sustain(1).release(4).room(.7).size(.9).gain(.12)
  .sections("coda")

sketches.name: Lento for Flute and Organ
sketches.description: A slow flute melody in E-flat sings in the centre while the organ chords underneath turn their interaural phase, from once every five seconds to just under once a second, so the harmony drifts gently around inside your head. The organ opens alone, the flute sings three times (an octave higher the second time) and a last Eb chord turns once every ten seconds as it fades. All rates stay well below 3 Hz.
sketches.source:
setcpm(56/4)

// The organ alone, the flute three times (an octave higher in the middle), then a last chord
song("intro@4 lento@8 lento'@8 lento@8 coda@4", "once")
// Steady, then a ritardando over the last four bars
tempomap("0:14 28:14 32:10")

// irate turns the phase between the ears, in turns per second, like a very slow rotating speaker
// All rates stay below 3 Hz, so no pulse warning is needed: Eb, Cm, Ab, Bb
organ: note("<[eb3,g3,bb3] [c3,eb3,g3] [ab2,c3,eb3] [bb2,d3,f3]>")
  .s("sawtooth").timbre("organ").irate("<.2 .4 .8 .4>")
  .lpf(1200).attack(.5).sustain(.9).release(1).space("church").gain(.14)
  .exceptSections("coda")

// The flute, the same in both ears
flute: note("<[g4@3 bb4] [c5@2 bb4 g4] [ab4@3 c5] [bb4@4] [eb5@3 d5] [c5@2 g4@2] [c5 bb4 ab4 c5] [bb4@2 d4@2]>")
  .s("sine").timbre("hollow").vib(5).vibdepth(.1)
  .attack(.08).sustain(.7).release(.6).room(.5).gain(.22)
  .sections("lento").variant(x => x.add(12).gain(.15))

// The pedal walks the roots, centred
pedal: note("<eb2 c2 ab1 bb1>").s("sawtooth").timbre("organ").lpf(450)
  .attack(.3).sustain(.8).release(1).space("church").gain(.2)
  .exceptSections("coda")

// The last Eb chord, pedal included, turns once every ten seconds as it fades
final: note("[eb2,eb3,g3,bb3]").slow(4).s("sawtooth").timbre("organ").irate(.1)
  .lpf(1000).attack(.5).sustain(.9).release(3).space("church").gain(.15)
  .sections("coda")

sketches.name: Wandering Etude
sketches.description: A flowing piano etude in E minor where nothing is panned, yet the brightness drifts from ear to ear: a low-pass on each ear alone sweeps in opposite directions every eight bars. The inner voices are thinner on the right, where a high-pass cuts their body. The inner voices and bass open, the etude runs three times (its figures reversed the second time) and an E minor chord comes to rest in the middle.
sketches.source:
setcpm(80/4)

// Inner voices and bass alone, the etude three times (reversed in the middle), then a last chord
song("intro@4 etude@16 etude'@16 etude@8 coda@4", "once")
// Steady, then a ritardando over the last four bars
tempomap("0:20 44:20 48:14")

// A low-pass on each ear alone, sweeping in opposite directions every eight bars
// The level stays put; only the brightness wanders: Em, C, Am, B
etude: n("0 2 4 2 7 4 2 4").add("<0 -2 -4 -3>").scale("E:minor").transpose(12)
  .s("triangle").timbre("bright")
  .lcutoff(saw.range(600, 4000).slow(8)).rcutoff(isaw.range(600, 4000).slow(8))
  .attack(.003).decay(.4).sustain(.1).release(.4).room(.4).gain(.22)
  .sections("etude").variant(x => x.rev())

// A high-pass on the right ear only: the inner voices sound fuller on the left
inner: note("<[g3,b3] [g3,c4] [a3,c4] [f#3,b3]>").s("sawtooth").rhcutoff(1100)
  .lpf(1600).attack(.6).sustain(.8).release(1).room(.4).gain(.1)
  .exceptSections("coda")

// The left hand on the roots, the same in both ears
left: note("<e2 c2 a1 b1>").s("triangle").timbre("soft")
  .attack(.005).decay(1.2).sustain(.2).release(1).gain(.24)
  .exceptSections("coda")

// The last chord: both ears at the same brightness, at rest in the middle
final: note("[e2,b2,g3,b3,e4]").slow(4).s("triangle").timbre("soft")
  .lcutoff(2000).rcutoff(2000)
  .attack(.005).decay(3).sustain(.1).release(4).room(.5).gain(.22)
  .sections("coda")

sketches.name: Invention for Two Ears
sketches.description: A two-part invention in C with one voice in each ear: the upper line leans right and the lower line left through a level difference, and on every fourth bar they trade places. In the middle pass the voices also trade octaves but keep their ears, so you still follow each one by its side. A slower final C closes the piece. Easy to follow, and a gentle way to hear counterpoint as two separate lines.
sketches.source:
setcpm(84/4)

// The invention, a pass where the voices trade octaves, the invention again and a final C
song("invention@16 invention'@8 invention@16 coda@2", "once")
// Steady, then a ritardando into the last chord
tempomap("0:21 38:21 42:15")

// ild makes the right ear louder; earswap flips the ears on the steps marked 1
// The upper voice leans right, the lower left; every fourth bar they swap
// In the primed pass they cross in pitch but keep their ears
upper: note("<[c5 d5 e5 f5 d5 e5 c5 g5] [c6@2 b5 c6 d6@2 g5@2] [a5 g5 f5 e5 d5 f5 e5 d5] [c5@4 ~@4]>")
  .s("triangle").timbre("bright").ild(6).earswap("<0 0 0 1>")
  .attack(.003).decay(.3).sustain(.2).release(.2).room(.4).gain(.22)
  .sections("invention").variant(x => x.add(-12))
lower: note("<[c3@2 e3@2 g3@2 e3@2] [g2@2 b2@2 g3@2 b2@2] [f2@2 a2@2 g2@2 b2@2] [c3@4 g2 a2 b2 c3]>")
  .s("square").pw(.25).lpf(1800).ild(6).earswap("<1 1 1 0>")
  .attack(.003).decay(.3).sustain(.3).release(.2).room(.4).gain(.14)
  .sections("invention").variant(x => x.add(12))

// The final C: the upper voice on the right, the lower on the left
upperend: note("[c5,e5]").slow(2).s("triangle").timbre("bright").ild(6)
  .attack(.003).decay(2).sustain(.1).release(2).room(.5).gain(.18).sections("coda")
lowerend: note("c3").slow(2).s("square").pw(.25).lpf(1400).ild(6).earswap(1)
  .attack(.003).decay(2).sustain(.1).release(2).room(.5).gain(.12).sections("coda")

sketches.name: Reading Room Nocturne
sketches.description: Headphones on: a nocturne in A in a quiet reading room. The air of the room is wide and diffuse, a fire crackles to your left, a clock ticks on the right and rain falls outside, behind the glass. The left hand opens alone, the song is sung three times (an octave higher the second time) and the piece slows to a held A as the room goes on around you.
sketches.source:
setcpm(58/4)

// The left hand alone, the song three times (an octave higher in the middle), then a held A
song("intro@4 nocturne@8 nocturne'@8 nocturne@8 coda@4", "once")
// Steady, then a ritardando over the last four bars
tempomap("0:14.5 28:14.5 32:10")

// Left hand: broken chords through A, F#m, D and E
left: note("<[a2 e3 c#4 e3 a3 e3 c#4 e3] [f#2 c#3 a3 c#3 f#3 c#3 a3 c#3] [d2 a2 f#3 a2 d3 a2 f#3 a2] [e2 b2 g#3 b2 e3 b2 g#3 b2]>")
  .s("triangle").timbre("soft").attack(.005).decay(.9).sustain(.1).release(1.2)
  .lpf(1800).room(.5).gain(.26)
  .exceptSections("coda")

// Right hand: the song, in the centre of your head
right: note("<[e5@3 d5 c#5@2 e5@2] [c#5@4 b4@2 a4@2] [a4@3 b4 d5@2 f#5@2] [e5@6 ~@2]>")
  .s("sine").fm(.8).fmh(2).attack(.01).decay(1.4).sustain(.2).release(1.5)
  .room(.6).gain(.3)
  .sections("nocturne").variant(x => x.add(12).gain(.2))

// The last chord, left to ring in the room
final: note("[a2,e3,c#4,e4,a4]").slow(4).s("triangle").timbre("soft")
  .attack(.005).decay(3).sustain(.1).release(4).lpf(1800).room(.6).gain(.24)
  .sections("coda")

// The air of the room: unrelated noise in each ear, wide and enveloping
air: s("pink").slow(8).icorr(.15).hpf(600).lpf(3000).gain(.025)

// A fire on your left, a clock on your right, rain beyond the window
fire: s("fire").slow(4).intensity(.25).density(5).azimuth(-60).distance(3).gain(.14)
clock: s("tick ~ tick ~").azimuth(70).distance(4).gain(.05)
rain: s("rain").slow(4).intensity(.35).occlude(.6).gain(.16)

sketches.name: Beta Allegretto
sketches.description: A baroque allegretto in G for violin, harpsichord continuo and cello, over a very quiet 14 Hz binaural drone in the beta range. The continuo sends its lows to one ear and its highs to the other; together, and in mono, it sounds whole. The continuo and cello open, the violin plays its runs, turns them backwards for a pass and returns before a slower G chord ends the piece. The player asks before playing, as with any steady pulse.
sketches.source:
setcpm(96/4)

// Continuo and cello alone, the violin's runs, the runs reversed, the runs again, a last chord
song("intro@4 allegretto@16 allegretto'@8 allegretto@16 coda@2", "once")
// Steady, then a ritardando into the last chord
tempomap("0:24 42:24 46:16")

// The violin runs in eighths through G, C, D and G, the same in both ears
violin: n("0 2 4 2 5 4 2 4").add("<0 3 4 0>").scale("G:major").transpose(12)
  .s("sawtooth").vib(5).vibdepth(.08).lpf(3000)
  .attack(.02).decay(.2).sustain(.5).release(.1).room(.4).gain(.18)
  .sections("allegretto").variant(x => x.rev())

// earsplit("bands") puts the continuo's lows in one ear and its highs in the other
continuo: note("<[g3,b3,d4] [c4,e4,g4] [d4,f#4,a4] [g3,b3,d4]>").struct("x ~ x ~")
  .s("square").pw(.15).earsplit("bands").splitfreq(800)
  .decay(.25).sustain(0).lpf(3200).room(.3).gain(.12)
  .exceptSections("coda")

// The cello on root and fifth, centred
cello: note("<[g2 d2] [c3 g2] [d3 a2] [g2 d2]>").s("sawtooth").lpf(700)
  .attack(.04).sustain(.6).release(.3).room(.4).gain(.22)
  .exceptSections("coda")

// The last G chord, bowed and held
final: note("[g2,d3,b3,g4]").slow(2).s("sawtooth").vib(5).vibdepth(.06).lpf(1400)
  .attack(.3).sustain(.8).release(3).room(.5).gain(.14)
  .sections("coda")

// A 14 Hz binaural beat in the beta range: each ear is detuned by 7 Hz. Keep it very quiet,
// and quieter still in the intro and coda
drone: note("[g2,d3]").slow(4).s("sine").binaural(14)
  .attack(3).sustain(1).release(4).gain(bysec("intro:.06 coda:.05 *:.08"))

sketches.name: Closing the Books
sketches.description: The end of the session: a slow harp minuet in B-flat floating a little above your head, over a 2 Hz binaural drone in the delta range, below the rates that trigger a pulse warning, with crickets far away. The drone and bass open, the minuet plays with its repeat, drops an octave for a pass, returns once more and slows to a last floating Bb chord.
